newsitem.title: FRANCE: France fires state firm boss in privatisation row.
newsitem.headline: France fires state firm boss in privatisation row.

text.p: The French government fired GAN state insurance firm chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud on Wednesday following a fall-out over a scrapped bank privatisation and named Didier Pfeiffer from rival insurer UAP to replace him.
Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said a decree removing Bonnaud had been approved at a cabinet meeting.
UAP said in a statement Finance minister Jean Arthuis had named UAP vice-president Pfeiffer as successor at Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN).

The rare firing a state-appointed chairman by decree followed a government decision in mid-November to scrap a tender for the privatisation of GAN bank subsidiary CIC and charges by Arthuis that Bonnaud and CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt failed to promote the sell-off.
Lamassoure declined to comment on the removal of Bonnaud, who argued that heeding a government call to resign amounted to an admission of guilt and he believed he had done no wrong.
Pfeiffer, who has served a string of successive chairmen in over 24 years at UAP, will not be replaced as vice-president.

Pfeiffer is widely expected to sack Yoncourt, who infuriated Arthuis in October by declaring on television in the middle of the CIC privatisation tender that a French bank takeover could spell death for CIC, a grouping of 11 regional banks.

The plan to sell 67 percent of CIC, or Credit Commercial et Industriel, ran into fierce resistance from local politicians and staff and the government received only two offers -- from French banks BNP and Societe Generale.

Societe Generale's offer was ruled ineligible by France's privatisation commission on the grounds that it did not meet the terms imposed by the government, which include respecting CIC's regional identity and insurance sales ties with parent GAN.

CIC is valued at around 14 billion francs ($2.71 billion) on GAN's books but banking analysts have said the terms and conditions imposed by the government were sure to take a toll on the price offered by suitors.
Arthuis says he is determined to privatise CIC and recently called on the bosses of the 11 regional banks to provide him with ideas for alternatives by the end of the year.
Bonnaud, who took over at the helm of GAN in 1993, crossed swords with Prime Minister Alain Juppe this year when Juppe tried to name one of his closest advisors at the head of CIC.
Juppe backed down amid a storm of media controversy and Bannaud got his way to appoint Yoncourt as CIC boss.

UAP chairman Jacques Friedmann said in a statement that an internal appointee, Eric Giuily, would work directly with him on group general management but that Pfeiffer's post of vice-president was not being filled.
